passages.text: Woe to those at ease in Zion and those secure on Mount Samaria, the distinguished ones of the foremost nation, to whom the house of Israel comes.
passages.sermon:
This message is from the LORD, the God of Hosts.
He speaks to the people of Israel.
He warns the leaders in Zion.
He warns those who feel safe on Mount Samaria.
These people are important among the nations.
The house of Israel comes to them.
Woe to those who are at ease in Zion.
Woe to those who trust in their security on Mount Samaria.
passages.original: ה֚וֹי הַשַּׁאֲנַנִּ֣ים בְּצִיּ֔וֹן וְהַבֹּטְחִ֖ים בְּהַ֣ר שֹׁמְר֑וֹן נְקֻבֵי֙ רֵאשִׁ֣ית הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וּבָ֥אוּ לָהֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Cross over to Calneh and see; go from there to the great Hamath; then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are you better than these kingdoms? Is their territory larger than yours?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God tells them to look at other kingdoms.
Go to Calneh and see it.
Go from there to the great city of Hamath.
Go down to Gath, a city of the Philistines.
Ask yourselves this question.
Are you better than these kingdoms?
Is their land greater than your land?
passages.original: עִבְר֤וּ כַֽלְנֵה֙ וּרְא֔וּ וּלְכ֥וּ מִשָּׁ֖ם חֲמַ֣ת רַבָּ֑ה וּרְד֣וּ גַת־ פְּלִשְׁתּ֗ים הֲטוֹבִים֙ מִן־ הַמַּמְלָכ֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה אִם־ רַ֥ב גְּבוּלָ֖ם מִגְּבֻלְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: You dismiss the day of calamity and bring near a reign of violence.
passages.sermon:
The people in Zion and Samaria feel safe and important.
They do not fear trouble.
They push away thoughts of disaster.
They do not believe a day of calamity will come.
They bring violence closer.
They allow evil to rule among them.
passages.original: הַֽמְנַדִּ֖ים לְי֣וֹם רָ֑ע וַתַּגִּישׁ֖וּן שֶׁ֥בֶת חָמָֽס׃

passages.text: You lie on beds inlaid with ivory, and lounge upon your couches. You dine on lambs from the flock and calves from the stall.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel live in luxury.
They lie on beds decorated with ivory.
They stretch out and relax on their couches.
They eat lambs taken from the flock.
They eat calves chosen from the stall.
passages.original: הַשֹּֽׁכְבִים֙ עַל־ מִטּ֣וֹת שֵׁ֔ן וּסְרֻחִ֖ים עַל־ עַרְשׂוֹתָ֑ם וְאֹכְלִ֤ים כָּרִים֙ מִצֹּ֔אן וַעֲגָלִ֖ים מִתּ֥וֹךְ מַרְבֵּֽק׃

passages.text: You improvise songs on the harp like David and invent your own musical instruments.
passages.sermon:
The people play music on the harp.
They make up songs as they play.
They act like David, who was a musician.
They invent new musical instruments for themselves.
passages.original: הַפֹּרְטִ֖ים עַל־ פִּ֣י הַנָּ֑בֶל כְּדָוִ֕יד חָשְׁב֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם כְּלֵי־ שִֽׁיר׃

passages.text: You drink wine by the bowlful and anoint yourselves with the finest oils, but you fail to grieve over the ruin of Joseph.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel live in luxury and self-indulgence.
You drink wine from large bowls.
You anoint yourselves with the finest oils.
You do not grieve over the ruin of Joseph.
You do not care about the suffering of your people.
passages.original: הַשֹּׁתִ֤ים בְּמִזְרְקֵי֙ יַ֔יִן וְרֵאשִׁ֥ית שְׁמָנִ֖ים יִמְשָׁ֑חוּ וְלֹ֥א נֶחְל֖וּ עַל־ שֵׁ֥בֶר יוֹסֵֽף

passages.text: Therefore, you will now go into exile as the first of the captives, and your feasting and lounging will come to an end.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
He warns them about their pride and sinful living.
He says, “You will go into exile first.
You will be the first among the captives.
Your feasting will stop.
Your lounging will end.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֛ן עַתָּ֥ה יִגְל֖וּ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ גֹּלִ֑ים וְסָ֖ר מִרְזַ֥ח סְרוּחִֽים׃פ

passages.text: The Lord GOD has sworn by Himself—the LORD, the God of Hosts, has declared: “I abhor Jacob’s pride and detest his citadels, so I will deliver up the city and everything in it.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD is the LORD.
He is the God of Hosts.
He has sworn by Himself.
He says this:
“I hate the pride of Jacob.
I hate Jacob’s strongholds.
I will hand over the city.
I will give up everything in the city.”
passages.original: נִשְׁבַּע֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה בְּנַפְשׁ֗וֹ נְאֻם־ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י צְבָא֔וֹת מְתָאֵ֤ב אָֽנֹכִי֙ אֶת־ גְּא֣וֹן יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְאַרְמְנֹתָ֖יו שָׂנֵ֑אתִי וְהִסְגַּרְתִּ֖י עִ֥יר וּמְלֹאָֽהּ׃

passages.text: And if there are ten men left in one house, they too will die.
passages.sermon:
God is speaking through the prophet Amos.
God warns the people of Israel.
God says disaster will come.
If ten men remain alive in one house, they will all die.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־ יִוָּ֨תְר֜וּ עֲשָׂרָ֧ה אֲנָשִׁ֛ים בְּבַ֥יִת אֶחָ֖ד וָמֵֽתוּ׃

passages.text: And when the relative who is to burn the bodies picks them up to remove them from the house, he will call to one inside, “Is anyone else with you?” “None,” that person will answer. “Silence,” the relative will retort, “for the name of the LORD must not be invoked.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Hosts.
He has sworn by Himself to judge Israel.
A relative comes to burn the bodies in the house.
He picks up the bones to remove them from the house.
He calls to someone who is deep inside the house.
He asks, “Is anyone else with you?”
The person answers, “None.”
The relative says, “Be silent.”
He says this because they must not mention the name of the LORD.
passages.original: וּנְשָׂא֞וֹ דּוֹד֣וֹ וּמְסָרְפ֗וֹ לְהוֹצִ֣יא עֲצָמִים֮ מִן־ הַבַּיִת֒ וְאָמַ֞ר לַאֲשֶׁ֨ר בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֥י הַבַּ֛יִת הַע֥וֹד עִמָּ֖ךְ וְאָמַ֣ר אָ֑פֶס וְאָמַ֣ר הָ֔ס כִּ֛י לֹ֥א לְהַזְכִּ֖יר בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: For the LORD gives a command: “The great house will be smashed to pieces, and the small house to rubble.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
\r\nThe LORD gives a command.
\r\nThe LORD will destroy the houses.
\r\nThe LORD will smash the great house into pieces.
\r\nThe LORD will break the small house into rubble.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ מְצַוֶּ֔ה וְהִכָּ֛ה הַבַּ֥יִת הַגָּד֖וֹל רְסִיסִ֑ים וְהַבַּ֥יִת הַקָּטֹ֖ן בְּקִעִֽים׃

passages.text: “Do horses gallop on the cliffs? Does one plow the sea with oxen? But you have turned justice into poison and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood— you who rejoice in Lo-debar and say, ‘Did we not take Karnaim by our own strength?’
passages.sermon:
The prophet Amos speaks to the people of Israel.
He asks a question.
Do horses run on rocky cliffs?
No, horses do not run on cliffs.
He asks another question.
Does anyone plow the sea with oxen?
No, people do not plow the sea with oxen.
Amos explains the meaning.
You have changed justice into poison.
You have made the fruit of righteousness taste bitter like wormwood.
You rejoice over nothing.
You say, “Did we not take Karnaim by our own strength?”
You trust in your own power.
You are proud of your own achievements.
You do not honor God.
passages.original: הַיְרֻצ֤וּן בַּסֶּ֙לַע֙ סוּסִ֔ים אִֽם־ יַחֲר֖וֹשׁ בַּבְּקָרִ֑ים כִּֽי־ הֲפַכְתֶּ֤ם לְרֹאשׁ֙ מִשְׁפָּ֔ט וּפְרִ֥י צְדָקָ֖ה לְלַעֲנָֽה׃ הַשְּׂמֵחִ֖ים לְלֹ֣א דָבָ֑ר הָאֹ֣מְרִ֔ים הֲל֣וֹא בְחָזְקֵ֔נוּ לָקַ֥חְנוּ לָ֖נוּ קַרְנָֽיִם׃

passages.text: For behold, I will raise up a nation against you, O house of Israel,” declares the LORD, the God of Hosts, “and they will oppress you from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of the Arabah.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Hosts.
The LORD speaks to the house of Israel.
The LORD says, "I will raise up a nation against you."
This nation will come against you, people of Israel.
They will oppress you.
They will oppress you from Lebo-hamath.
They will oppress you to the Brook of the Arabah.
passages.original: כִּ֡י הִנְנִי֩ מֵקִ֨ים עֲלֵיכֶ֜ם בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י הַצְּבָא֖וֹת גּ֑וֹי וְלָחֲצ֥וּ אֶתְכֶ֛ם מִלְּב֥וֹא חֲמָ֖ת עַד־ נַ֥חַל הָעֲרָבָֽה׃ס
